notes.animal_notes:
Otto is a sweet, low-energy boy who loves people and has never met someone he didn't like. He is very sniff-forward and likes to spend his time outside going on slow, sniffy walks. Athletic runs are not his speed - he will lie down in the grass instead. He likes all kinds of pets and pats and will lean on people if they let him. He particularly likes his ears being rubbed. He is very food motivated and plays nicely with other dogs.

Things to know

Otto loves being around people and gets a bit nervous if left by himself. He also is not the most steady on slippy surfaces and can get insecure if he does slip. He makes a "tea kettle whine" if he is nervous but rarely ever barks (we've heard it only 2 times in 9 months). Loud noises can startle him. He does not enjoy getting picked up, but will jump on platforms if he is interested. He has never shown an interest in toys and doesn't want to learn how to play fetch. Instead, he enjoys a puzzle toy or foraging for snacks in the grass. He is a bit older, so he gets pretty tired towards the end of the day and at home is asleep by 6:30 each day, having had many hours of napping throughout the day.

Training
Otto has passed his AKC Canine Good Citizen (CGC) test! He knows "sit," "down," "paw," "spin," "place," and "heel". He mostly will do "leave it," but not 100% of the time. His rewards cue is "Good!." His recall cue is "Touch" and stick out your hand so he can boop it with his nose. He enjoys learnings new tricks and is eager to please.

Bathroon

He typically poops once at around 8 am every day on his morning walk. It typically takes about 10-15 minutes of walking before he will poop. He likes to poop near trees and will face the tree. He pees about 4 times a day, at 8 am, 12 pm, 3 pm, and 10 pm.

notes.owner_notes: Juno is a sweet 9 year old, 13 lb chihuaua mix. Her super power is comfort — she finds and the softest, coziest spot in every room and loves to be near humans to cuddle. She is the sweetest, most gentle pup, and I feel so lucky that we found each other back in 2018. In addition to human attention, she enjoys long spry walks under the palm trees, sitting at windows watching nature, and playing with her nylabones and dog friends! Juno is a respectful, house trained, quiet dog. She is a momma and she radiates that vibe. Juno is a warm addition to every pack she joins!

But if she has sudden unexplained bruising, particularly on her belly or gums, please call the VCA ASEC internal medicine department ASAP.
